sub_topics.name: Introduction to Quicksort and Pivot Definition
sub_topics.description: Today we're going to learn quicksort. Like merge sort, quicksort is a recursive algorithm. However, when you think of quicksort, I want you to think of the word pivot. A pivot is simply one of the items in the array that meets the following three conditions after we sorted it. First, the pivot is in its correct position in the final sorted array. 1Correct position in final, sorted array | 2. Items to the left are smaller | 3. Items to the right are larger This means that all items to the left are smaller and all items to the right are larger. Let's look at an example.

Now starting at the right we see that 1 is item from right. Let's swap item from left with item from right.

sub_topics.name: Pivot Selection Strategy, Pseudocode, and Time Complexity
sub_topics.description: One important question is how do we choose the pivot? This makes a large difference in the performance of the algorithm, as we want to choose a pivot that divides the array in half, or as close as possible, to even out the work. One popular method is called median of three. In this method we look at the first, middle, and last elements of the array. We sort them properly and choose the middle item as our pivot. We're making the guess that the middle of these three items could be close to the median of the entire array, and as you can see it's not too far. Here's the pseudocode for quicksort. Worst case: O(n²) | Average case: O(nlogn) Thank you for watching! | Please subscribe and share.
